title: Grilled Reuben Sandwiches for the Crew
displayTitle: Grilled Reuben Sandwiches for the Crew
seoTitle: Grilled Reuben Sandwiches for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Reuben night—corned beef char on the griddle, rye pressed crisp for ten
subtitle: Grilled corned beef, sauerkraut, Swiss, and rye for ten
description: Thick-cut corned beef grills on the flat-top until charred, stacks on rye with sauerkraut, Swiss, and Thousand Island, and presses until melty and crisp.

steps.title: Warm sauerkraut
steps.instruction: Drain sauerkraut and warm in a small pan at 140°F with pinch of caraway. Hold warm.

steps.title: Heat griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 425°F for beef, then reduce to 375°F for pressing.

steps.title: Grill corned beef
steps.instruction: Grill thick corned beef slices 2 minutes per side until charred edges and warmed through.

steps.title: Hold beef
steps.instruction: Hold grilled corned beef covered at 170°F in hotel pans.

steps.title: Build reubens
steps.instruction: Spread Thousand Island on rye. Layer Swiss, corned beef, sauerkraut, more Swiss. Butter outer rye.

steps.title: Press sandwiches
steps.instruction: Press reubens at 375°F 3 minutes per side until rye is crisp and cheese melts.

steps.title: Hold wrapped
steps.instruction: Hold finished reubens wrapped in foil at 170°F up to 20 minutes.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: One reuben per firefighter with pickle chips on the side.

proTips: Drain sauerkraut well—wet kraut steams bread instead of crisping.
Thick-cut corned beef survives the press; deli-thin shreds.
Caraway in warmed kraut adds classic reuben aroma.
tonightSpread: Grilled reuben sandwiches with pickle chips.
Potato chips or dill pickle spear.
leftovers: Corned beef hash with sauerkraut next morning.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Reubens feel like deli night at the hall. Corned beef grills fast on the griddle, holds at 170°F, and presses in minutes between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Grill corned beef slices at 425°F, 2 minutes per side. Hold at 170°F up to 30 minutes. Press reubens at 375°F, 3 minutes per side.
